races.name: Sodexo Live! 2yo Series EBF Maiden Fillies' Stakes (Hamilton Park 2yo Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Little Lady Karen
runners_data.note: Unraced Dark Angel filly with outstanding breeding connections making debut for in-form Burke stable
runners_data.comment: £68,000 yearling; from a top northern stable and could have a big say on debut
runners_data.spotlight: 52,000gns foal, £68,000 yearling; first foal; dam twice-raced half-sister to 1m Group 1 winner Accidental Agent, out of 5f 2yo/7f winner (RPR 90); this Dark Angel newcomer takes on rivals who have shown plenty of promise but she's from a top northern stable and could have a big say.

runners_data.name: Meennaa
runners_data.note: Prominent runner likely to get uncontested lead, showed ability on Kempton debut and 31 days freshening should help
runners_data.comment: Clear second on last month's debut at Kempton; this Lambourn raider has to be respected
runners_data.spotlight: 225,000gns yearling whose dam was a very talented 2yo; backed into 4-1 when clear second on last month's debut at Kempton (6f, AW); there have been mixed messages from that form but it was a promising start to her career and she's travelled from Lambourn for this second start; has to be respected.

runners_data.name: Angels Passing
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who showed promise in Listed company on debut, needs stronger pace to be effective
runners_data.comment: Eyecatching fourth on debut in Listed race at York and she could have plenty more to offer
runners_data.spotlight: 18-1 and slowly away before keeping on well for fourth of ten on debut in a Listed race at York (5f, good) three weeks ago; this 130,000euros yearling could have plenty more to offer tackling 6f; strong claims.

runners_data.name: Jazz Queen
runners_data.note: Inconsistent hold-up filly with place form, Jack Nicholls' 5lb claim valuable but needs pace setup
runners_data.comment: Disappointing at Haydock but went close at Chester previously; in the mix if back on song
runners_data.spotlight: Disappointing 15-8 shot at Haydock (6f, good to soft) a fortnight ago on her third start; however, prior to that she went close in a maiden at Chester (5.5f, good) and can be in the mix if back on song.

races.paceDynamic: Meennaa will take them along from the front with her prominent style, setting a sustainable pace in this small field of four. With no other confirmed pace pressers, she'll get an easy lead through the early stages without being harassed. The two hold-up horses Angels Passing and Jazz Queen will need to rely on the pace being strong enough to set up their late runs, but with only Meennaa dictating terms, they may find themselves with too much to do. This race shape clearly favours front-running and prominent runners who can capitalize on the uncontested early pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Meennaa Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Meennaa gets the soft lead she's likely to receive in this small field
scenarios.body: She can dictate fractions and kick clear turning for home, with the hold-up horses struggling to bridge the gap in time. Her debut second suggests she has the class to take advantage of favorable pace dynamics.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Rally
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes stronger than expected or Meennaa doesn't stay the trip
scenarios.body: Jazz Queen and Angels Passing can use their late-running styles to sweep past a tiring leader in the final furlong. Both showed promise on recent debuts and could benefit from race fitness.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Newcomer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Little Lady Karen shows immediate ability on debut with her strong breeding
scenarios.body: The Dark Angel filly with Group 1 connections could surprise, particularly if positioned prominently behind Meennaa. Her expensive yearling price and pedigree suggest latent ability waiting to be unlocked.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Meennaa goes too fast early and all four finish in a bunch
scenarios.body: The race becomes a scramble in the final furlong with any of the quartet capable of prevailing. Form horses Jazz Queen and Angels Passing would have slight edges in a messy finish.

watchPoints.text: Meennaa getting too easy a lead early - if she's not put under any pressure through the first half-mile, she could prove hard to catch
Little Lady Karen's market moves given her debut status - any significant support would suggest stable confidence in immediate ability
Angels Passing breaking more alertly than her slow York debut - improved gate speed would enhance her chances significantly
Jazz Queen's consistency issues continuing - she's been disappointing favorite before and could underperform again
Track conditions firming up further - any shift toward firm ground could impact the two hold-up horses' effectiveness

races.name: Morton Fraser Macroberts LLP Handicap

runners_data.name: Novak
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who ran well at Ayr over 7f but faces a drop back to 6f and potential traffic issues from his style
runners_data.comment: 7f runner-up at Ayr recently; return to 6f isn't an obvious plus but it's a stiff finish
runners_data.spotlight: Went close to ending a losing sequence when runner-up at Ayr (7f, good to firm) recently; slow ground would pose a question and the drop back to 6f isn't an obvious plus, but the stiff finish helps to compensate; not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Kelpie Grey
runners_data.note: Prominent runner on a dangerous low mark with a long losing streak but showed respectability last time for in-form Goldie stable
runners_data.comment: His losing sequence continues but on a dangerous mark and he ran respectably last time
runners_data.spotlight: His losing sequence goes back 16 races to May 2024 and his form has gone the wrong way; however, he's dropped to a dangerous mark and ran respectably when fifth of nine over 7f at Ayr a fortnight ago (11-8 favourite), when shaping as though the return to 6f may help; not ruled out.

runners_data.name: Thunderstorm Katie
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare stepping up from 5f wins to 6f with strong finishing kick but needs luck from the back
runners_data.comment: Has kept on well over 5f on last two starts and the return to 6f is well worth exploring
runners_data.spotlight: Two 5f wins last October (good/AW) and runner-up over that trip on last two starts (good/good to firm), finishing well each time and shaping as though this return to 6f is well worth exploring; could play a leading role if conditions suit; best turf efforts have come on good/good to firm.

runners_data.name: Impressor
runners_data.note: Hold-up veteran with excellent Hamilton record but underwhelming recent form away from this track
runners_data.comment: Underwhelming since promising reappearance run but he has a strong record at Hamilton
runners_data.spotlight: Underwhelming on his three starts since promising reappearance run at Doncaster in March; however, he has a strong record at Hamilton and is running here for the first time this season; slow ground would be a positive.

runners_data.name: Iris Dancer
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with strong Hamilton record (9 of 10 career runs here) but mixed 2024 form
runners_data.comment: Her form has been mixed this season but she's a well handicapped course specialist
runners_data.spotlight: Her form has been mixed this season and she was soundly beaten at Carlisle last time; however, she's running at Hamilton for the first time this year and nine of her 11 wins have come over C&D; she's 10lb lower than when winning here last August and could bounce back with a bold show.

runners_data.name: Carlton And Co
runners_data.note: Front-running type who may have needed his reappearance run 24 days ago and has good second-half season record
runners_data.comment: Down the field on reappearance but may have needed it; three wins in second half of 2025
runners_data.spotlight: Down the field on last month's reappearance at Catterick but may have needed that run; won three times in the second half of last year (6f/7f, good/AW) and is not discounted; has run well on good to soft going.

runners_data.name: Belsito
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won twice over C&D last September and showed return to form with close fourth at Southwell
runners_data.comment: Won two in a row over C&D last September; slow ground would be a major boost to his claims
runners_data.spotlight: Won two in a row over C&D last September (good to soft/soft) and returned to form with very close fourth at Southwell (6f, AW) in April on his second start of the season; slow ground would be a major boost to his claims.

runners_data.name: Invincible Ruby
runners_data.note: Prominent runner struggling this season after July 2023 win but warrants market check for potential revival
runners_data.comment: Won last July when 6lb higher but she's struggled so far this season
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Catterick (7f, good to firm) last July when 6lb higher; a market check is advised but she's struggled so far this season.

runners_data.name: Wish This
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won in first-time blinkers last November but well below that level in three 2024 starts
runners_data.comment: Won at Newcastle (6f, AW) last November but well below that level this spring
runners_data.spotlight: Won in first-time blinkers at Newcastle (6f, AW) last November but he's been well below that level in cheekpieces/blinkers on AW/turf on his three outings this spring.

runners_data.name: Pickersgill
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning from 58-day break after AW wins but faces step back to turf racing
runners_data.comment: AW win in March on fourth yard start; one to consider, especially if slow ground prevails
runners_data.spotlight: Beaten a neck at Wolverhampton (7f, AW) in March on third stable start then went one better at Southwell (7f, AW); won on turf at the Curragh (6f, soft) last March and this stiff 6f could be a good fit; she's one to consider, especially if slow ground prevails.

races.paceDynamic: Carlton And Co and Iris Dancer will dispute the early lead, with Carlton And Co likely to establish control given his stronger recent form. The pace should be honest but not frantic, with four prominent runners (Kelpie Grey, Belsito, Invincible Ruby, Wish This) creating congestion behind the leaders through the middle stages. The hold-up horses (Novak, Thunderstorm Katie, Impressor) will need luck in running as traffic becomes an issue approaching the final 2f. This race shape favours horses with prominent or leading positions who can avoid the scramble behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leaders dominate throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Carlton And Co or Iris Dancer establish uncontested control
scenarios.body: The pace becomes steady enough for the front pair to maintain their advantage, with the prominent quartet unable to make serious inroads. Hold-up horses get into traffic trouble and never threaten seriously.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent surge late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace becomes too strong between the leaders
scenarios.body: Carlton And Co and Iris Dancer weaken in the final furlong, allowing the prominent runners to sweep past. Belsito and Kelpie Grey benefit most from their tactical positioning.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-up heroes strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely or traffic clears unexpectedly
scenarios.body: The early tempo becomes pedestrian or the hold-up horses find clear runs at the crucial moment. Thunderstorm Katie's 5f to 6f step-up or Novak's recent Ayr form could prove decisive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete pace meltdown
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders go too hard and die dramatically
scenarios.body: Carlton And Co and Iris Dancer burn each other out in a speed duel, creating a stop-start race. The entire field comes together in a bunch finish where anything can happen.

watchPoints.text: Watch for traffic problems developing 2f out as four prominent runners (Belsito, Kelpie Grey, Invincible Ruby, Wish This) converge behind the leaders
Monitor early pace battle between Carlton And Co and Iris Dancer as both need to establish position but could burn each other out
Check market moves for Invincible Ruby who has been struggling but connections may know something given stable's recent form
Watch Thunderstorm Katie's position entering final 2f as she needs clear running from hold-up position to utilise her 5f speed
Observe Impressor's jumping from the stalls as his Hamilton record suggests track suits but recent away form is concerning

races.name: Weatherbys Global Stallions Handicap

runners_data.name: Obito
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 20-day break who may have needed his reappearance run and could strip fitter today
runners_data.comment: Two wins last season (including here) and he may have needed his reappearance outing
runners_data.spotlight: Always towards the rear on reappearance over C&D (good) three weeks ago but may have needed that run; won twice last summer (1m/1m2f, good; including here) and he's on a competitive mark on last autumn's form (including on soft ground); he can be in the mix if bouncing back.

runners_data.name: Pearl Eye
runners_data.note: Hold-up type fully 12lb lower than when winning the Spring Mile and has shown recent form for new trainer Jim Goldie
runners_data.comment: Ran well in defeat at Ayr last month on first two starts for yard and is on the shortlist
runners_data.spotlight: Awarded the Spring Mile at Doncaster (1m, good to soft) last March and he's fully 12lb lower today; ran well in defeat at Ayr last month on first two starts for this yard (1m/1m1f, good to firm) and he's on the shortlist.

runners_data.name: Qitaal
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who was denied clear run when second last time and could benefit from better racing luck
runners_data.comment: Without a win since September 2024 but denied a clear run when 2nd at Leicester recently
runners_data.spotlight: Inconsistent and without a win since September 2024; however, he was denied a clear run when second of six at Leicester (1m2f, good to firm) recently and can be in the shake-up if backing that up; versatile ground-wise.

runners_data.name: Mr Lincoln
runners_data.note: Prominent style but has been focusing on hurdles recently and 61 days since last flat run creates fitness doubt
runners_data.comment: Twice placed over hurdles this spring and today's trip may be a good fit in this code
runners_data.spotlight: Twice placed over hurdles this spring (2m1f, good to soft/good), with a heavy defeat on the Flat at Musselburgh (1m6f, soft) in between; however, it's possible this shorter trip will be a better fit for him in this code.

runners_data.name: Highland Olly
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner who made all to win twice in April but disappointed when racing wide at York
runners_data.comment: Made all twice in a row in April; down the field at York since but could bounce back
runners_data.spotlight: Made all twice in a row in April (8.3f/1m, good); down the field at York (7f, good) but that was in a big field and he raced wide; could bounce back with a bold show if conditions suit (well beaten on soft going last November but displayed signs of promise on such ground early in career).

runners_data.name: Zowal
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 58-day break but won at Pontefract last time and could be well handicapped
runners_data.comment: Won over 1m at Pontefract latest & there's every chance he'll be fine at this longer trip
runners_data.spotlight: Encouraging reappearance run in the Spring Mile at Doncaster (1m, good to soft) and he built on that to win at Pontefract (1m, good to soft); there's every chance that he'll be fine at this longer trip and he's respected.

runners_data.name: Penelope's Sister
runners_data.note: Hold-up mare who won here in 2024 but has been well beaten on both starts this spring
runners_data.comment: She's below her last winning mark but has been well beaten on both outings this spring
runners_data.spotlight: Won here in 2024 and added three wins at Ayr last year; she's below her last winning mark but has been well beaten on both outings this spring and a major turnaround is necessary.

runners_data.name: Draupnir
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who showed promise when third on reappearance and finished fifth here three weeks ago
runners_data.comment: Reappeared with promising third at Thirsk and he's better than he showed here last time
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Thirsk (7f, soft) last September and reappeared with promising third there (7f, good) in April; kept on for fifth over this C&D (good) three weeks ago in a race that favoured those ridden more prominently, and the first-time hood may not have suited (left off today); possible player.

runners_data.name: Tee Aitch Aye
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who won over course and distance last September but has been tailed off recently
runners_data.comment: C&D winner who is one to watch in the betting but tailed off on both starts this season
runners_data.spotlight: Won over C&D (soft) last September when 1lb higher and he's one to watch in the betting, especially if the ground is on the slow side; however, he's been tailed off on both starts this season.

races.paceDynamic: Highland Olly stands alone as the only confirmed front runner and will be allowed an uncontested lead in this small field. The prominent runners Qitaal, Mr Lincoln and Draupnir will track behind but none are pace forcers, creating a steady tempo through the early stages. With most runners preferring to hold up including Obito, Pearl Eye, Zowal, Penelope's Sister and Tee Aitch Aye, this sets up a tactical affair with a strong gallop only developing in the final 3-4 furlongs. This sustainable pace scenario strongly favours hold-up horses and closers who can produce their best turn of foot in the straight.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustainable Pace Suits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Highland Olly gets an easy lead and the pace doesn't quicken until the final 3f
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get the perfect setup to unleash their finishing kicks with plenty left in the tank. Obito and Pearl Eye can time their challenges perfectly while Zowal and Tee Aitch Aye benefit from the strong gallop.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Qitaal or Draupnir press Highland Olly earlier than expected creating moderate pace
scenarios.body: The increased tempo stretches the field more but still allows the better horses in behind to close effectively. Qitaal's recent second when denied a clear run suggests he's ready to strike.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Highland Olly gets such soft fractions that he has plenty left for the finish
scenarios.body: The uncontested leader kicks clear entering the straight and holds off all challengers with his superior tactical position. His two wins in April when making all show this tactic can work.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so slow that it becomes a sprint from the 2f pole
scenarios.body: The race becomes a lottery with positioning crucial and several horses getting in each other's way. The handiest horses with natural speed benefit most from the messy finish.

watchPoints.text: Highland Olly could get such an easy lead that he's impossible to peg back despite his York disappointment
Watch Pearl Eye's price as he's 12lb lower than his Spring Mile winning mark and could be overpriced
Obito may have needed his reappearance run 20 days ago and could show significant improvement today
Market support for Qitaal would suggest connections expect him to get a clearer run than at Leicester
Any price drift on Zowal despite his Pontefract win would be concerning given his 58-day absence

races.name: Weatherbys Digital Solutions Clyde Handicap

runners_data.name: Diego Ventura
runners_data.note: Prominent runner dropping in grade from Group/Listed level with solid recent York form, though 21 days off may need the run
runners_data.comment: Not beaten far when seventh of 18 in handicap at York and this is less competitive
runners_data.spotlight: He's tended to ply his trade in Group and Listed races and he was a Listed winner at Longchamp (7f, good to soft) last May; beaten just under 4l when seventh of 18 at York (1m, good) three weeks ago on his first handicap start and this is less competitive; could be in the mix.

runners_data.name: Al Mubhir
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from disappointing Australian campaign but trainer Kevin Ryan struggling for winners this season
runners_data.comment: Well treated on old form but soundly beaten on stable debut following a stint in Australia
runners_data.spotlight: Listed win at Sandown in July 2024 and well treated on that form; however, he drew a blank during his 2025 Australian campaign and was soundly beaten on last month's stable debut in the Thirsk Hunt Cup; something to prove.

runners_data.name: Botanical
runners_data.note: Failed to settle at Newmarket last time but showed promise in Lincoln fourth, prominent style suits if jockey can get him to relax
runners_data.comment: Promising 4th in the Lincoln on stable debut and he's better than he showed at Newmarket
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten at Newmarket last month but he failed to settle and looked unsuited by the track; prior to that he was a promising fourth in the Lincoln at Doncaster (1m, good to soft) on his stable debut and there's mileage in his mark on his old form; has won over C&D and he's one to consider.

runners_data.name: Theoryofeverything
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose four wins all came on soft ground, may find this good to firm surface too quick
runners_data.comment: Ran well when fifth of 18 at York last month and slow ground would aid this course winner
runners_data.spotlight: Ran well when fifth of 18 at York (1m, good) three weeks ago on his second start of the season; his four wins (one here) have come on soft going so slower ground today would aid his cause; could be a contender.

runners_data.name: Altareq
runners_data.note: Front-runner showing improvement for Jim Goldie who has been in good form, promising third on comeback suggests fitness
runners_data.comment: Very lightly raced 4yo; promising third on stable debut at York & could take step forward
runners_data.spotlight: Went close in Newbury maiden (1m2f, good) last May on third and final outing for Gosdens and, having been detached early, he was a very promising third of 15 on his stable/handicap debut at York (1m2f, good) three weeks ago; well bred and could take a sizeable step forward from that latest effort.

runners_data.name: Eternal Force
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning after 68-day break having won three in a row post-gelding, class act but may need the run
runners_data.comment: Won final three starts last season and could build on respectable comeback run in Lincoln
runners_data.spotlight: Made it 3-3 since being gelded (good to firm/good to soft) when winning by 3l at Haydock (1m) last October; reappeared with respectable seventh of 21 in the Lincoln at Doncaster (1m, good to soft) and this lightly raced 4yo could build on that latest effort today; firmly in calculations.

runners_data.name: Two B Tanned
runners_data.note: Front-runner with excellent course record (headgear positive) who won five times last season and scored on reappearance
runners_data.comment: Made all at Musselburgh on reappearance; disappointing since but not written off
runners_data.spotlight: Front-runner who won five times last April-July (1m-1m1f) and improved again when making all at Musselburgh (1m, good) in April on her reappearance; well beaten at Redcar 11 days later when unpenalised and 8lb higher mark has now kicked in, but she's not written off; unproven on slow ground.

races.paceDynamic: Two B Tanned and Altareq will ensure a genuine gallop from the start, with both confirmed front-runners likely to dispute the early lead over this extended distance. The honest pace should create opportunities for prominent runners like Diego Ventura and Botanical to track the leaders, while hold-up horses Al Mubhir, Theoryofeverything and Eternal Force will need the pace to be strong enough to bring them into contention. Given the dual pace angle and stamina demands of 1m½f, this race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can sit close to the pace without getting embroiled in the early battle.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustained Gallop Favours Prominent
scenarios.trigger: If Two B Tanned and Altareq maintain a solid gallop without killing each other
scenarios.body: The honest tempo allows prominent runners to position perfectly and strike when the leaders weaken. Diego Ventura and Botanical are ideally placed to capitalize on their superior class.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Early Burn-Out Benefits Hold-Up
scenarios.trigger: If the two leaders go too fast early and collapse dramatically
scenarios.body: The strong early pace sets up perfectly for closers who can stay the extended trip. Al Mubhir and Eternal Force can use their hold-up styles to maximum advantage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If Two B Tanned or Altareq gets an uncontested lead and controls the tempo
scenarios.body: The leader dictates terms and has enough left to resist late challenges on the testing ground. Two B Tanned's course form gives her the edge in this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Tactical Affair
scenarios.trigger: If both leaders hesitate early or get into a speed duel that compromises both
scenarios.body: The race becomes stop-start which suits versatile types who can adapt tactically. Botanical's class tells in a scrappy finish.

watchPoints.text: Two B Tanned's early position crucial - if she gets first run on Altareq she could dictate terms throughout
Botanical's settling ability under inexperienced jockey Jack Nicholls will determine if he can use his class advantage
Eternal Force's fitness after 68-day layoff against horses who have recent runs under their belts
The pace battle between Two B Tanned and Altareq in the first two furlongs sets up the entire race shape
Theoryofeverything's action on this good to firm surface compared to his preferred soft conditions

races.name: Aspire Cleaning & Facilities Ltd Handicap

runners_data.name: Water Of Leith
runners_data.note: Hold-up style needs strong pace to be effective but recent form suggests he's below his Wolverhampton winning level.
runners_data.comment: AW winner in March but below that level in three subsequent starts
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Wolverhampton (6f, Class 5; 6-4 favourite) in March but below that level in three subsequent starts, 2l fifth of eight at Musselburgh (5f; 15-2) latest; vulnerable on those performances.

runners_data.name: Parisiac
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 216 days but his consistency at this trip and going gives him clear tactical advantage.
runners_data.comment: Lacks a recent run but he's consistent in the main and not handicapped out of it
runners_data.spotlight: Multiple winner who lacks a recent run but he's consistent in the main and not handicapped out of it; market could be informative.

runners_data.name: Call To Action
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits the likely pace scenario and his recent Pontefract second shows he's close to winning form.
runners_data.comment: Thirsk was disappointing but that was a Class 4, so this is easier
runners_data.spotlight: Ended 2025 with a win and better than ever when a close second of eight at Pontefract (5f, good) on reappearance; Thirsk was disappointing but that was a Class 4, so this is easier.

runners_data.name: Hi Lord
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won over course and distance last time with headgear removed, suggesting trainer has found the key.
runners_data.comment: Headgear removed and doubled his tally with a narrow win over C&D a month ago
runners_data.spotlight: Headgear removed and doubled his tally with a narrow win over C&D (good; 3lb lower) a month ago; consistency hasn't always been his forte but clearly a possible contender.

runners_data.name: Harb
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in excellent recent form with a course-and-distance win 17 days ago, though 4lb higher in weights.
runners_data.comment: Hit and miss but career win number nine when narrowly scoring at Carlisle 17 days ago
runners_data.spotlight: Hit and miss but it was career win number nine when narrowly scoring at Carlisle 17 days ago (5f, good), coming from off the pace; 4lb higher here.

runners_data.name: Lion's House
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who struggles on turf compared to Tapeta and lacks the tactical pace this race requires.
runners_data.comment: Tapeta is his surface and finished well behind in his last two races on turf
runners_data.spotlight: Has only won on Tapeta and spends a lot of his time at Newcastle; finished well behind in his last two races on turf.

races.paceDynamic: Parisiac is the sole confirmed pace-setter and should get an uncontested lead with Call To Action and Hi Lord sitting prominent but unlikely to press hard early. The lack of genuine speed horses means a moderate gallop is likely, setting up a finish where stamina and tactical positioning become crucial over pure speed. With three hold-up horses (Water Of Leith, Harb, Lion's House) relying on the race developing into a sprint, the sustainable pace should favor horses that can stay close enough to strike. This tactical setup strongly favors prominent racers who can track the leader without being caught in a messy finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Parisiac gets soft fractions and isn't pressed for pace early
scenarios.body: The moderate gallop plays into his stamina strengths and he can dictate terms throughout before finding enough in the final furlong. His consistency at this trip on similar going makes him hard to peg back when allowed to control the race.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Call To Action or Hi Lord can sit close enough behind the modest pace
scenarios.body: They get the perfect stalking trip and can time their challenge to perfection when the race develops into a sprint finish. Both have shown finishing kicks at this distance and the shape suits their prominent style perfectly.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Charges
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely steady and turns into a cavalry charge
scenarios.body: The race becomes a pure sprint from the 2f pole where Harb's recent course-and-distance form and finishing kick can be maximized. Water Of Leith's Wolverhampton win suggests he retains ability if getting the right race shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Parisiac goes too slow early and multiple horses converge simultaneously
scenarios.body: The race becomes a messy affair where positioning and luck matter more than ability, potentially allowing an outsider to sneak through. This chaotic finish could suit any horse getting a clear run at the right moment.

watchPoints.text: Parisiac's market moves will be crucial given his 216-day absence - strong support would confirm connections expect him fresh and ready.
Call To Action's consistent prominent style could be perfectly suited if he can avoid the disappointing Thirsk effort.
Hi Lord's headgear removal last time coincided with his course-and-distance win and could signal continued improvement.
Harb's hold-up style needs the pace to develop properly but his recent Carlisle win shows he's in career-best form.
Water Of Leith's ability to overcome a 36-day break after his recent disappointing efforts at this level.

races.name: Sodexo Live! Events Handicap

runners_data.name: Sure And Stedfast
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner ideally suited to a strong pace scenario with good recent form at this track and distance
runners_data.comment: 3rd over 1m3f here last month and could play a leading role if seeing out this longer trip
runners_data.spotlight: Returned to form when third here (1m3f, good) last month on second run of the season; also effective on soft ground; could play a leading role if seeing out this longer trip, and there can be optimism on that score.

runners_data.name: Jujubella
runners_data.note: Closer who needs the strong gallop but arrives out of form and may struggle to reach previous best
runners_data.comment: Revival required but well handicapped and stable has won last two runnings of this race
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten last month on her two runs this year (1m2f/1m1f) and arrives with something to prove, but she's 4lb lower than when winning at Haydock (11.6f, good) last July and the step up in trip may be a positive; stable has won the last two runnings of this race with Two Auld Pals; not written off.

runners_data.name: Annandale
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning from 107-day absence, likely needs this run despite his C&D winning ability
runners_data.comment: Went close on AW in February when last seen but he may improve for this first run since
runners_data.spotlight: Five-time turf winner who went close at Wolverhampton (1m6f, AW) in February when last seen; not discounted but it's possible this 8yo will improve for this first run since; question mark about slow ground nowadays.

runners_data.name: Glasses Up
runners_data.note: Veteran front-runner who may struggle to match younger pace-setters but brings tactical know-how
runners_data.comment: Close third at Ayr two starts ago but that course brings out his best; well beaten since
runners_data.spotlight: 11yo who was a close third over 1m1f at Ayr two starts ago and is versatile trip-wise; however, Ayr brings out the best in him and he was well beaten at Musselburgh last time; 0-4 here, with last visit coming last June.

runners_data.name: Clansman
runners_data.note: Key pace angle having made all in recent AW wins but unproven on good ground, prefers softer
runners_data.comment: Two AW wins in the spring; six-time winner on turf, all those coming on soft/heavy going
runners_data.spotlight: Two AW wins from the front this spring (1m4f/2m), the latest at Southwell in April when last seen; he's a six-time winner on turf, with all those coming on soft/heavy going; claims enhanced if slow ground prevails.

runners_data.name: Kisiyra
runners_data.note: Prominent runner having first start for 363 days, complete unknown quantity but interesting yard switch
runners_data.comment: Ran pretty well on sole outing of last season but returns from another absence today
runners_data.spotlight: Ex-Irish 5yo who is 0-8; not beaten far when fourth of six at 66-1 at Thirsk (1m4f, good) last June on her stable debut and sole outing of the season, but she's back from another absence today and it may be best to look elsewhere; wears a first-time tongue-tie.

runners_data.name: Perseus Way
runners_data.note: Strong closer returning from hurdles with C&D winning form, but 258 days since last flat run
runners_data.comment: C&D winner who won over hurdles last month and there's lots to like about his claims
runners_data.spotlight: Won over C&D (good to soft) last September and he's just 1lb higher today; won over hurdles at Hexham (2m4f, soft) last month on his second start for this yard and there's lots to like about his claims.

runners_data.name: Gallus Norman
runners_data.note: In-form front-runner who made all last time and suits the likely strong gallop scenario
runners_data.comment: Easily made all at Musselburgh recently and this unexposed 7yo has to be respected
runners_data.spotlight: Improved form when runner-up on handicap debut at Musselburgh (1m4f, good) in April and easily made all back there (2m, good) a fortnight ago; he enjoyed the run of the race last time but a 6lb rise isn't harsh in view of this unexposed 7yo's dominance; has to be respected.

races.paceDynamic: Clansman, Gallus Norman, and Glasses Up will create a fierce early battle for the lead, with all three having strong front-running tendencies and recent form showing they need to be prominent. This triple threat up front guarantees a strong gallop over 1m5f, particularly as Clansman and Gallus Norman have been making all recently and won't want to give ground. The sustained pace will test stamina reserves in the final two furlongs, creating a searching examination. This race shape strongly favors hold-up horses who can finish with one late run, as the pace-setters will likely weaken after their early exertions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners engage in a speed duel through the first mile
scenarios.body: The relentless gallop will drain the leaders' stamina reserves, setting up the race perfectly for closers. Sure And Stedfast and Perseus Way can time their challenges to perfection as the pace falls apart.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Gallus Norman or Clansman gets loose on the lead while the others fight
scenarios.body: The successful front-runner will have enough left to resist late challenges on this testing track. Their recent winning form from the front gives them the tactical edge to control the tempo.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Kisiyra can secure an ideal tracking position behind the speed battle
scenarios.body: The 5yo will have the perfect setup to strike in the straight while avoiding the early pace war. Her trainer change and long absence could mask improved form ready to be unleashed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Holds Together
scenarios.trigger: If the three leaders cooperate and settle into a rhythm rather than fighting
scenarios.body: The front-runners maintain enough stamina to repel the closers' challenges in a tactical finish. Glasses Up's experience and versatility could prove decisive in a sprint finish.

watchPoints.text: Watch if Clansman handles the good ground as all his turf wins came on soft conditions
Monitor Perseus Way's fitness after 258 days off the flat, though his recent hurdles win suggests readiness
Observe if Kisiyra shows any market confidence given her 363-day absence and stable switch
Check if Glasses Up can match the pace of younger front-runners Clansman and Gallus Norman early
Watch for Annandale's response to returning after 107 days, could improve significantly for the run

races.name: Hampton By Hilton Hamilton Park Handicap

runners_data.name: Sophiesticate
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits the likely pace scenario, returning to a more suitable trip after disappointing over shorter at Ayr
runners_data.comment: Return to form needed but below last winning mark and back up to a more suitable trip
runners_data.spotlight: Below par on final two starts last year and same story on recent reappearance over 1m at Ayr; however, she's back up to a more suitable trip today and is 6lb below her last winning mark; not written off.

runners_data.name: Dandy's Angel
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who may find this longer trip more suitable than her recent inadequate 8.4f efforts at Beverley
runners_data.comment: 9yo for whom a return to form is needed but the step back up in trip could help
runners_data.spotlight: Beverley specialist who hasn't been at the top of her game over 8.4f there on her two starts this season; however, that trip is probably inadequate nowadays and she has a reduced mark to work with back up in trip; has won over C&D and this 9yo is not written off.

runners_data.name: Ravenswell
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose poor recent run over 2m can likely be excused as a prep run after 71 days off
runners_data.comment: Tailed off on reappearance but over 2m; might not be a forlorn hope back down in trip
runners_data.spotlight: He will have something to prove if slow ground prevails and he was tailed off on his recent reappearance over 2m at Musselburgh; however, that was his first run beyond 1m3f and he went close over that trip at Carlisle last August, when 2lb higher; might not be a forlorn hope back down in trip.

runners_data.name: Hijo De La Luna
runners_data.note: Prominent racer returning after 71 days off with visor that helped him win last time out
runners_data.comment: Won on AW in February but hasn't shone since (AW/hurdles); needs to get back on track
runners_data.spotlight: Won a classified race at Wolverhampton (9.4f, AW) in February in a first-time visor; however, down the field at Lingfield (1m2f, AW) in March and well beaten back over hurdles in April; needs to get back on track.

runners_data.name: Recobella
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse in excellent recent form with two good efforts at Doncaster over similar trips this season
runners_data.spotlight: Just one win from her 17 starts but she's run really well in defeat at Doncaster on both turf outings this season (1m2f/1m4f, good to soft/good) and there's every chance she'll be bang there once more.

runners_data.name: Sugarpiehoneybunch
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner wearing a hood who won this race last year and may have needed her recent reappearance
runners_data.comment: No return to form on reappearance but may have needed it and she won this last year
runners_data.spotlight: Soundly beaten on final three starts last season and same story on reappearance in April; however, she might have needed that latest outing and she won this last year; shouldn't be discounted.

runners_data.name: Falaise Blanc
runners_data.note: Prominent style wearing a hood but well below his best form from last season's Newcastle win
runners_data.comment: Of interest on his form last August/September but well below that level so far this season
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Newcastle (1m2f, AW) last August and runner-up at Musselburgh (1m4f, good to soft) next time; however, he's been well below that level so far this season and a major turnaround is necessary.

runners_data.name: Ivynator
runners_data.note: Prominent runner making seasonal debut after 307 days off, hard to assess current ability
runners_data.comment: 2nd over hurdles last May but hasn't got competitive on his four starts since (one Flat)
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up over hurdles last May but this 8yo has struggled to get competitive on his four starts since, one of those being on the Flat; races for the first time since last September and others make greater appeal.

runners_data.name: Wath Court
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with fading tendencies wearing a tongue-tie, longstanding maiden with poor recent form
runners_data.comment: Longstanding maiden who has been well beaten on all four starts this year
runners_data.spotlight: Longstanding maiden who has been well beaten on all four starts this year and would be a surprise winner today.

runners_data.name: Storm On Jura
runners_data.note: Hold-up type prone to fading who has been well beaten in all three handicap attempts
runners_data.comment: 4yo who has raced only six times but has been well beaten in her three handicaps
runners_data.spotlight: 4yo who has raced only six times but has been well beaten in her three handicaps, the latest her reappearance at Musselburgh in April.

runners_data.name: Uncle Liam
runners_data.note: Prominent/leading style making him the likely pace-setter, stamina unproven at this 1m4f trip
runners_data.comment: Lots to prove regarding current form/stamina; could stage revival when back on slow ground
runners_data.spotlight: 11-race maiden who arrives with plenty to prove regarding current form and stamina (untested at trip); however, his pedigree provides optimism regarding him staying and he could stage a revival when back on slow ground.

races.paceDynamic: Uncle Liam is the only confirmed front-runner in this field, meaning he can dictate terms without early pressure from other pace-setters. With most runners holding up or sitting mid-division, Uncle Liam will get an uncontested lead through steady fractions over this 1m4f trip. The prominent racers like Hijo De La Luna and Falaise Blanc will track behind, while the majority including Sophiesticate, Recobella, and Ravenswell will come from off the pace. This tactical setup strongly favours hold-up horses who can benefit from the sustainable tempo and have something left for a finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Stays
scenarios.trigger: If Uncle Liam gets easy fractions and sees out the trip
scenarios.body: The 4yo gets first run on his rivals turning for home and his stamina questions are answered positively in a race run to suit front-runners. The hold-up horses find the pace was just quick enough to blunt their finishing kicks.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Benefit
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is too slow for the distance
scenarios.body: Sophiesticate and Recobella get the perfect tactical setup to use their proven stamina, with Ravenswell also dangerous despite his recent poor run. The backmarkers sweep past Uncle Liam in the final furlong as his lack of early pressure backfires.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine but not too strong
scenarios.body: Hijo De La Luna and Falaise Blanc get the best of both worlds, avoiding the early speed battle but staying close enough to strike. They pick up Uncle Liam inside the final quarter-mile while the hold-up horses leave their runs too late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the main fancies underperform on ground or distance
scenarios.body: Sugarpiehoneybunch repeats her 2023 course success or Dandy's Angel finds the longer trip suits despite poor recent Beverley form. The pace collapse allows an unfancied runner to pick up the pieces from an unlikely position.

watchPoints.text: Uncle Liam could get an uncontested lead that proves impossible to peg back if his stamina holds out
Sophiesticate and Recobella are the main dangers from off the pace if the early gallop becomes too pedestrian
Hijo De La Luna wearing the visor that helped him win last time but faces a significant layoff of 71 days
Storm On Jura and Wath Court both show fading tendencies that could be exposed over this longer trip
The pace could collapse completely given only Uncle Liam wants to go forward, setting up a sprint finish
